mainTopic: The end of פרק כיצד משתתפין and the opening of פרק כל גגות: whether roofs are one רשות, רבי מאיר's ten-טפחים גזירה, and the רב–שמואל dispute about carrying on a single roof.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous chapter. The ban on pouring water applies only when no עירוב was made, and רב אשי explains that it is a גזירה so people will not carry water vessels out of their houses. After the הדרן, a new chapter begins with a משנה about roofs. רבי מאיר says all the city's roofs are one רשות, unless a roof is ten טפחים higher or lower than its neighbor. The חכמים say each roof is its own רשות, and רבי שמעון joins roofs, courtyards and קרפיפות together for objects that began שבת there. The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר has the ten-טפחים exception, and אביי answers that it is only a גזירה because of a mound in the רשות הרבים. אביי limits this גזירה to fixed objects. When challenged from a wall between courtyards, רב ששת explains that רבי מאיר allows carrying only through the doorways. Finally, רב and שמואל argue about carrying within a single roof according to the חכמים, and the argument depends on גוד אסיק מחיצתא. The גמרא then begins quoting the משנה to test that dispute, and the test continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ban applies only without a joint עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the previous משנה's ban on pouring water to a case where no עירוב was made. If a עירוב was made, everyone may pour.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only taught this ban when the residents did not make a עירוב. But if they did make a עירוב, they are all permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is narrowing the previous משנה. The rule that residents without a pit (עוקה) may not pour water applies only when there is no עירוב between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה split the residents into two groups: those who dug a עוקה may pour, and those who did not may not. The גמרא now says this split only exists without a עירוב. Once a עירוב joins them, the worry behind the ban disappears and both groups may pour.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this (a phrase that limits a rule to a specific case)
They made an עירוב (a joint arrangement that merges domains for carrying)
They are permitted

phrases.english: They only taught this when they did not make an eruv,
phrases.notes: This refers back to the משנה's ban on residents who had no pit.

phrases.english: but if they made an eruv, they are all permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This qualifies the משנה from the previous daf, which is not part of this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on residents without a עוקה applies only when there is no עירוב. With a עירוב, everyone may pour.

steps.title: Why is pouring forbidden without a עירוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ban in the case where no עירוב was made.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when they did not make a עירוב, what is the reason they may not pour?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why pouring is forbidden when there is no עירוב. It is setting up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring water is not obviously carrying, so the ban needs a reason. The question focuses on what danger the missing עירוב creates.

keyTerms.meaning: And when (introducing a case to examine)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And when they did not make an eruv,
what is the reason they may not pour?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לֹא עֵירְבוּ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This asks for the reasoning behind the limited ban stated in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the ban when there is no עירוב.

steps.title: רב אשי: a protective decree against carrying vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the ban is a rabbinic גזירה. Without it, people might carry containers of water from their houses into the shared area.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is a גזירה, in case people come to carry vessels out of the houses to there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question. Pouring water itself is not the problem; the חכמים banned it to stop people from carrying water vessels out of their houses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a עירוב, carrying from a house into the shared area is forbidden. If people were allowed to pour, they might bring containers of water out of the house to pour them there. With a עירוב that carrying is allowed, so there is no reason for the גזירה. This explains the distinction made in Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to protect against a real prohibition
Lest / perhaps
To take out
Vessels of the houses

steps.whatToRemember: The ban is only a גזירה against carrying. That is why a עירוב, which permits the carrying, also removes the ban.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is a decree, lest they come
to take out vessels from the houses to there.
phrases.notes: "There" means the shared area where the water is poured.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי גְּזֵירָה דִּילְמָא אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question asked in Step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban is a גזירה, in case people carry vessels from their houses into the shared area without a עירוב.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter of כיצד משתתפין
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing formula for פרק כיצד משתתפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, כיצד משתתפין.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter ends here, marked by the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the legal argument. It only marks that the chapter is finished and that a new chapter follows.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the formula said when finishing a chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you, "How do we join" (Keitzad Mishtatfin)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This closes the chapter whose last discussion ended in Step 3.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: all the city's roofs are one domain
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter's משנה opens with רבי מאיר. He holds that all the roofs of a city are one רשות, unless a roof is ten טפחים higher or lower than its neighbor.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All the roofs of the city are one רשות, as long as no roof is ten טפחים higher or ten טפחים lower. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins. רבי מאיר rules that a person may carry from roof to roof across the city even without a עירוב, as long as the roofs are close in height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People rarely move things between roofs, so the חכמים did not forbid carrying between them without a עירוב. רבי מאיר still forbids carrying to a roof that is ten טפחים higher or lower than its neighbor. Step 10 explains that this is only a rabbinic גזירה; that roof is not truly a separate domain.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Roofs
One domain
Provided that
Ten handbreadths (the standard height that separates areas)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר allows carrying from a house onto a roof. He only treats the roofs, among themselves, as one area.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All the roofs of the city
are one domain,
provided that there is no roof
ten handbreadths higher or ten handbreadths lower,
phrases.notes: Higher or lower compared to the roof next to it.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כָּל גַּגּוֹת הָעִיר רְשׁוּת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new chapter and a new topic begin here.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the city's roofs are one רשות for carrying, unless a roof differs in height from its neighbor by ten טפחים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the chapter's main dispute about how roofs relate to one another for carrying on שבת.

steps.title: The Sages: each roof is its own domain
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. They hold that each roof is a separate רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: Each and every roof is a domain of its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give the opposing view. In their opinion, a person may not carry from one roof to another without a עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, each roof belongs to its own house, so it is a separate area. Its height compared to the neighboring roof makes no difference. Carrying between roofs therefore needs a עירוב between the houses.

keyTerms.meaning: And the חכמים say (introducing the opposing view)
Each and every one
On its own / by itself

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד רְשׁוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: each and every one is a domain in and of itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד רְשׁוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This disputes רבי מאיר's ruling in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each roof is its own separate רשות, so carrying between roofs requires a עירוב.

steps.title: A third view: roofs, courtyards and enclosed lots are all one area
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that roofs, courtyards and קרפיפות together form one domain. This applies only to objects that were in those areas when שבת began, not to objects that were inside the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: roofs, courtyards and enclosed lots are all one domain for objects that were in them when שבת began. They are not one domain for objects that were inside the house when שבת began.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third opinion, from רבי שמעון. He is even more lenient than רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר made all the roofs one domain. רבי שמעון goes further and joins roofs, courtyards and קרפיפות together. He limits this to objects that 'rested' in those areas at the start of שבת. An object that started שבת inside a house, even after it was brought out, may not be moved from one of these areas to another without an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: An enclosed lot or yard that is not used for living, usually outside the town's houses
Courtyards shared by several houses
Objects that were already in that place when שבת began

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not say you can carry anything at all between these areas. His leniency only covers objects that were outdoors when שבת began. Objects from inside the house are still restricted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea of 'where an object started שבת' as a factor in carrying, which comes up again later in the פרק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Both roofs and courtyards
and enclosed lots —
they are one domain
for objects that were in them when Shabbat began,
phrases.notes: 'Rested' (שבתו) means where the object was at the start of שבת.

phrases.english: but not for objects that were inside the house when Shabbat began.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the משנה's dispute between רבי מאיר and the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roofs, courtyards and קרפיפות are one domain for objects that rested in them at the start of שבת, but not for objects that rested in the house.

steps.title: The scholars agree the רבנן's view makes sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a scene: אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין are sitting with אביי. They say the view of the רבנן is easy to understand: residents are divided on the roofs just as they are on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין were sitting, and אביי was sitting with them. They said: The view of the רבנן makes sense. Just as residents are divided into separate domains down below, so too they are divided up above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the scene and agrees that the רבנן's view is logical. This is a setup: the word בשלמא tells us a question about the other opinion is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן reason that each house is its own domain on the ground. So each roof, which sits on top of a separate house, should also be its own domain. This logic is accepted. The problem will be with רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense that…' — admits one side is clear before asking about the other side
Residents are divided (each lives in his own separate domain)
Below (on the ground, in the houses) / above (on the roofs)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people here. אביי בר אבין is one of the brothers. The אביי sitting with them is the famous אביי, who answers in step 10.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Abaye bar Avin was sitting
and Rabbi Ḥanina bar Avin,
and Abaye was sitting beside them,
and they sat and said:
Granted, the Rabbis hold
that just as residents are divided below,
so residents are divided above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה by explaining the reason behind the חכמים' view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן's view rests on the idea that division on the ground carries up to the roofs.

steps.title: Either way, רבי מאיר's view seems not to fit
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask what רבי מאיר holds. If residents are divided above, why are the roofs one domain? If they are not divided, then even a roof ten טפחים higher or lower should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי מאיר, what does he hold? Suppose he holds that residents are divided above just like below. Then why are the roofs one domain? Suppose he holds they are not divided, because everything above ten טפחים counts as one domain. Then even a roof ten higher or ten lower should be allowed too!
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars challenge רבי מאיר with a two-sided question. Neither possible reason seems to match his whole ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one (roofs are divided) clashes with his main rule that all roofs are one domain. Option two (roofs are not divided) clashes with his exception for a ten-טפחים height difference. So his ruling looks inconsistent: lenient in general, yet strict for the ten-טפחים case.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he hold? (What is his reasoning?)
If… and if… (a two-sided question where both sides cause a problem)
Above ten טפחים from the ground

phrases.english: But Rabbi Meir, what does he hold?
If he holds:
just as residents are divided below,
so residents are divided above,
why are they one domain?
And if he holds they are not divided,
because everything above ten handbreadths
is one domain —
then even a roof ten handbreadths higher
or ten lower should also be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After granting that the רבנן's view makes sense, the scholars turn to the difficulty in רבי מאיר's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה: all roofs are one domain, except where one roof is ten טפחים higher or lower than the next.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dilemma. If roofs are divided, his main rule fails. If they are not divided, his ten-טפחים exception has no reason.

steps.title: אביי: the ten-handbreadth rule is a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes רבי מאיר's principle. Even where two areas are really one domain, the חכמים may forbid carrying between them because it looks like a mound in the רשות הרבים. The ten-טפחים difference between roofs falls under the same גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: Haven't you heard what רב יצחק בר אבדימי said? רבי מאיר used to say: Anywhere you find two areas that are really one domain, the חכמים are strict. For example, a pillar in a private domain that is ten טפחים high and four wide: it is forbidden to rest a load on it. This is a גזירה because of a mound in the public domain. Here too, the rule for roofs is a גזירה because of a mound in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the dilemma. רבי מאיר holds that roofs are truly not divided. The ten-טפחים exception is only a rabbinic גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mound ten high and four wide inside a רשות הרבים is a real רשות היחיד, so moving things onto it is a Torah violation. To keep people from mixing up the cases, רבי מאיר forbids similar-looking moves even inside one real domain, like a tall pillar or a roof ten טפחים off from its neighbor. So the second side of the dilemma is correct, and the exception is explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Haven't you heard? (introduces a known teaching that solves the problem)
To adjust or rest a load on one's shoulder, using a surface to help
A rabbinic decree made to prevent a Torah violation
A mound (if 10 high and 4 wide in a public area, it counts as a private domain)
A pillar

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, all roofs really are one domain. The ban on a roof ten טפחים higher or lower is only a גזירה, so people won't confuse it with a mound in the רשות הרבים.
steps.confusionAlert: The pillar is inside a private domain, so resting a load on it is not a Torah problem at all. It is forbidden only because it looks like the mound case, where the Torah problem is real.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a broad principle of רבי מאיר: he makes a גזירה even inside one real domain, whenever a setup looks like a true Torah case of moving between domains.

phrases.english: Abaye said to them:
Have you not heard

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי,
phrases.english: that which Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said,
Rabbi Meir would say:
Any place that you find
two domains that are really one domain,
for example, a pillar in a private domain
ten handbreadths high and four wide —
it is forbidden to adjust a load on one's shoulder upon it,
a decree because of a mound in the public domain.
Here too,
phrases.notes: Now the same idea is applied to the roofs.

phrases.english: it is a decree because of a mound in the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ אַבָּיֵי: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 9 by taking its second side and explaining the exception as a rabbinic גזירה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Takes one side of the dilemma (roofs are not divided) and explains the exception as a rabbinic decree, backed by a known teaching of רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ten-טפחים exception seemed to show that רבי מאיר holds roofs are truly divided, which would contradict his main rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Roofs are not truly divided. Carrying between roofs with a ten-טפחים difference is banned only by a גזירה, because it looks like moving onto a mound in the רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The scholars conclude that even portable objects are included
steps.stepSummary: From אביי's answer, the scholars assume that even a mortar or a tub ten טפחים high would fall under רבי מאיר's גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this that the rule applies even to a mortar, and even to a tub.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars draw a conclusion from אביי's answer in Step 10. Their conclusion is too broad, and the גמרא is setting up אביי's correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that a ten-טפחים height difference is forbidden because it looks like a mound in the רשות הרבים. The scholars took this to mean that any object ten טפחים high counts, even a movable household item like a mortar or an overturned tub. If so, one could not move things from the courtyard floor onto such an object.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (introduces an assumption, often a mistaken one)
A mortar, a heavy vessel used for pounding
A large tub or vat

steps.confusionAlert: 'סְבוּר מִינָּהּ' usually signals an assumption the גמרא is about to correct. Do not treat this as the final halacha.

phrases.english: They understood from this
phrases.notes: The scholars from Step 8 draw a conclusion from אביי's answer.

phrases.english: even a mortar, and even a tub.
phrases.notes: Movable objects ten טפחים high would also count as a 'mound'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a broad inference from אביי's explanation of רבי מאיר's גזירה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Assumed: the גזירה applies even to movable objects ten טפחים high, such as a mortar or tub.

steps.title: אביי limits the rule to fixed objects
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes his teacher: רבי מאיר's גזירה covers only fixed objects, like a pillar or a millstone base, because people treat them as permanent.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: This is what the Master said. רבי מאיר spoke only about a pillar or the base of a millstone, because a person gives them a fixed place.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects the scholars' broad conclusion. The rule covers only objects that stay in one fixed place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mound in the רשות הרבים is permanent. So the גזירה only applies to things that are similarly fixed, such as a pillar or a millstone base, which people rarely move. A mortar or a tub gets moved around, so it does not resemble a mound, and the חכמים made no גזירה about it.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what the Master said (quoting one's teacher, here רבה)
A pillar
The raised base of a millstone
Since, because
Gives them a fixed, permanent place

steps.whyThisMatters: This step defines what counts as a 'mound': being fixed in place, not just being ten טפחים high. That definition is exactly what the next challenge attacks.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ אַבָּיֵי, הָכִי אָמַר מָר:
phrases.english: Abaye said to them: The Master said as follows:
phrases.notes: 'מָר' is אביי's teacher, רבה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir only said this
about a pillar and the base of a millstone,
phrases.notes: Heavy items that stay in one place.

phrases.english: since a person fixes a place for them.
phrases.notes: Because they are permanent, they resemble a mound in the רשות הרבים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ אַבָּיֵי, הָכִי אָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the overly broad inference of Step 11 by narrowing the גזירה to fixed objects.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the extension to movable objects. The basic גזירה from Step 10 still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The scholars ignored that a mound is permanent. Movable objects lack that feature, so they do not look like a mound.

steps.title: Challenge from the wall between two courtyards
steps.stepSummary: A wall between two courtyards is fixed. Yet רב יהודה says that for רבי מאיר all courtyards form one domain, which seems to allow carrying over the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: But consider a wall between two courtyards, which is fixed. And רב יהודה said: When you analyze it, according to רבי מאיר, roofs are one domain of their own, courtyards are one domain of their own, and enclosures are one domain of their own. Doesn't that mean it is allowed to move things over the wall?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's rule with a case that seems to contradict it: a fixed wall between two courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By אביי's rule, a fixed object ten טפחים high should be forbidden, like a mound. A dividing wall is fixed and tall. Yet רב יהודה says that for רבי מאיר all courtyards together form one domain. The גמרא assumes this means one may carry from courtyard to courtyard over the top of the wall, which contradicts אביי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But here is a case (introduces a counter-example)
A wall
When you analyze it, you will find
A domain of their own (all of that type together form one domain)
Is it not that...? (introduces the assumed meaning behind the challenge)
To carry or move objects

steps.confusionAlert: 'גגין רשות לעצמן' here does NOT mean each roof is separate. It means all roofs together are one domain, separate from the courtyards. Likewise all courtyards together are one domain, and all enclosures together are one domain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge forces the גמרא to explain exactly how רבי מאיר lets people carry between courtyards. The answer, in Step 14, is through the openings, not over the wall.

phrases.english: But there is a wall that is between two courtyards,
phrases.notes: The counter-example.

phrases.english: which is fixed, and yet Rav Yehuda said:
phrases.notes: The wall fits אביי's 'fixed' standard.

phrases.english: When you analyze it, according to Rabbi Meir:
phrases.notes: רב יהודה is explaining רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: roofs are a domain of their own,
phrases.notes: All roofs together form one domain.

phrases.english: courtyards are a domain of their own,
phrases.notes: All courtyards together form one domain, so one may carry between them.

phrases.english: enclosures are a domain of their own.
phrases.notes: All קרפיפות together form one domain.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, דִּשְׁרֵי לְטַלְטוֹלֵי דֶּרֶךְ כּוֹתֶל!
phrases.english: What, is it not that it is permitted to carry over the wall?!
phrases.notes: Carrying over a fixed wall ten טפחים high would contradict אביי's rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the definition from Step 12 with a fixed object, a wall, that seems to be permitted.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's (רבה's) rule that a fixed object ten טפחים high is forbidden under רבי מאיר's גזירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wall is fixed and tall, so it should be forbidden. Yet רב יהודה's statement that all courtyards are one domain for רבי מאיר implies that carrying over the wall is allowed.

steps.title: The courtyards are one domain only through the doorways
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers the challenge from Step 13. רבי מאיר's ruling that all courtyards form one domain allows carrying only through doorways, not over the dividing wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רב ששת: No. רבי מאיר only allows bringing things in and taking them out through the doorways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13. רבי מאיר never allowed carrying over the fixed wall. He only allowed carrying from courtyard to courtyard through the doorways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 asked why a fixed wall between courtyards does not trigger רבי מאיר's גזירה. רב ששת says it does. Carrying over the top of the wall is still forbidden, and the 'one domain' ruling applies only to passing through the openings. So the rule that fixed objects fall under the גזירה stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Doorways or openings between areas
To bring in and to take out (carrying from place to place)
No. This rejects the assumption behind the question.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר lets you lift objects over the wall itself. 'One domain' here means passing through the doorways only.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said
Rav Sheshet said:
No, it means to bring in and to take out
phrases.notes: It is not saying the wall can be crossed over.

phrases.english: by way of the doorways.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of רבי מאיר's 'one domain' ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'All courtyards are one domain' means one may carry over the fixed wall, which would contradict the fixed-object גזירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Carrying is allowed only through the doorways. Over the wall, the גזירה still applies.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about carrying on one roof for the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים of the משנה, who say each roof is a separate domain. It then brings a dispute: רב says one may carry only four אמות on a roof, and שמואל says one may carry on the whole roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say each roof is its own domain. It was stated: רב said one may carry on it only within four אמות. שמואל said it is allowed to carry on the entire roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, the view of the חכמים in the משנה. It quotes their words and then brings an argument between רב and שמואל about carrying within a single roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים forbid carrying from one roof to another. The new question is about carrying inside one roof. רב is strict and allows only four אמות. שמואל allows carrying across the whole roof.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages say. This quotes the משנה.
A domain on its own
It was stated. This introduces a dispute between אמוראים.
Four cubits. This is the small area where one may always carry.
Throughout all of it (the entire roof)

phrases.english: And the Sages say
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד רְשׁוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: each and every one (roof) is a domain of its own.
It was stated: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בּוֹ אֶלָּא בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: one may carry on it only within four cubits,
and Shmuel said: it is permitted to carry throughout all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד רְשׁוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ. אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the חכמים' view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, רב allows carrying on a roof only within four אמות, and שמואל allows carrying on the entire roof.

steps.title: The dispute is only where the walls cannot be seen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the dispute. If the walls between the houses are visible, everyone allows carrying on the whole roof. They argue only when the walls are not visible from above.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the walls can be seen, everyone agrees. They argue when the walls cannot be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly which case רב and שמואל are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separate houses, whose walls stand out clearly, make each roof feel enclosed, so everyone allows carrying on the whole roof. The argument is about attached houses, where the roofs look like one long surface. In that case, nothing on the roof marks where one house ends and the next begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Partitions that are clearly visible
Partitions that are not visible (attached houses)
Everyone agrees; there is no dispute

phrases.english: With partitions that are noticeable —
everyone agrees (that one may carry on the whole roof).
Where they disagree is with partitions that are not noticeable.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּמְחִיצוֹת הַנִּיכָּרוֹת דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case of the dispute in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Visible walls: everyone allows carrying on the whole roof. Walls that cannot be seen: רב and שמואל disagree.

steps.title: The dispute depends on extending the walls upward
steps.stepSummary: רב does not use the principle of גוד אסיק מחיצתא, so he allows only four אמות. שמואל does use it, so he allows carrying on the whole roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב, who allows only four אמות, does not say 'extend the walls upward.' שמואל, who allows carrying on the whole roof, does say 'extend the walls upward.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side of the רב–שמואל dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גוד אסיק מחיצתא means we picture the walls of the house below rising up and closing in the roof. שמואל accepts this, so each roof counts as enclosed, and one may carry on all of it. רב does not accept it when the walls cannot be seen, so the roof stays open and carrying is limited to four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: Extend the partition upward. We treat the walls below as if they rise and enclose the area above.
To carry or move objects

steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל agree when the walls are visible. When the walls are hidden, the dispute depends on גוד אסיק מחיצתא: שמואל uses it and allows the whole roof, while רב does not and allows only four אמות.
steps.whyThisMatters: גוד אסיק מחיצתא is a key tool across the laws of עירובין and שבת for deciding when an area counts as enclosed.

phrases.english: Rav said: one may not carry on it
except within four cubits —
he does not say: 'Extend and raise the partition.'
And Shmuel said: it is permitted to carry throughout all of it —
because he says: 'Extend and raise the partition.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the dispute defined in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב rejects גוד אסיק מחיצתא for walls that cannot be seen, so he allows only four אמות. שמואל accepts it, so he allows the whole roof.

steps.title: The גמרא starts quoting the משנה to test the dispute
steps.stepSummary: Using the word תנן, the גמרא begins citing the חכמים of the משנה, who say that each roof is its own domain. This sets up a challenge to one side of the רב–שמואל dispute. The quote breaks off here, and the challenge itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: "And the חכמים say: each and every one…"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It begins quoting the חכמים of the משנה so it can test the רב–שמואל dispute against their exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 already quoted the חכמים to introduce the dispute. Here the גמרא brings the same words back for a new purpose, as a source to check against רב and שמואל. The word תנן tells us a quote from the משנה is coming, and the comparison to רב or שמואל follows in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: "We learned" — the signal that the גמרא is quoting a משנה
The Sages, the majority opinion in the משנה, who argue with רבי מאיר
"Each and every one" — here, each separate roof

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is just repeating Step 15. Step 15 quoted these words to introduce the dispute. Here the גמרא quotes them again in order to challenge one side of that dispute.

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah: And the Sages say:
phrases.notes: תנן introduces a quote from the משנה, here brought to test the dispute.

phrases.english: each and every one [roof]…
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud ("is a domain unto itself").

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 17 explained the reasoning behind רב and שמואל, the גמרא goes back to the משנה's wording to test their positions.
steps.kashyaTarget: One side of the רב–שמואל dispute about how far one may carry on a roof (completed on the next amud)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exact wording of the חכמים, that each roof is its own domain, will be examined to see whether it fits that side's ruling. The full attack is completed on the next amud.
